candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural influences on health, therapeutic relationships, client-centered psychosocial care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — culturally responsive mental health care
candidate.educational_objective: Provide individualized, culturally and linguistically responsive mental health care without stereotyping or imposing the nurse's own explanatory model.

options.A: Use the nurse's own explanatory model consistently so treatment decisions are not influenced by different cultural beliefs
options.B: Ask about the client's individual health beliefs, values, preferences, and communication needs and provide respectful care that responds to them when clinically feasible
options.C: Assume clients from the same cultural group share the same beliefs and select care based on expected group preferences
options.D: Avoid discussing cultural beliefs because high-quality mental health care should exclude personal explanatory models

candidate.rationale: The HHS National CLAS Standards call for effective, understandable, respectful quality care that responds to cultural health beliefs and practices, language, health literacy, and communication needs. HHS nursing CLAS training further emphasizes understanding and responding to each patient's experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences while addressing bias and stereotypes. B is correct because it individualizes culturally responsive care rather than imposing the clinician's beliefs or stereotyping the client by group membership.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Culturally responsive care should be respectful and responsive to each patient's cultural health beliefs/practices and communication needs, with individualized attention to experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences rather than stereotypes.
candidate.source_document_title: National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) in Health and Health Care; CLAS in Nursing
candidate.source_locator: National CLAS Standards — Principal Standard 1; CLAS in Nursing — program focus on understanding, respecting, and responding to patient experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences and awareness of bias/stereotypes
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Minority Health / Think Cultural Health
candidate.source_version_date: Current HHS CLAS standards and nursing program accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A nurse is planning mental health care for a client whose cultural health beliefs differ from the nurse's own. Which approach is most appropriate?
